notes: Access: direct HTTP fetch worked (Shopify storefront, robots.txt has no Claude-specific disallow, User-agent * Allow: /). Discovery: checked main nav/header, homepage, footer, /pages/sitemap nav page, a full /collections.json sweep of all 95 collections (title+handle scanned for clearance, outlet, final sale, last chance, end of line, discontinued, sale, festive-sale, etc.), and the site's own search for 'clearance' and 'outlet'. No collection anywhere in the 95-collection sweep is named/handled Clearance, Outlet, Final Sale, Last Chance, End of Line, or Discontinued. Two sale-worded candidates were found and opened: (1) 'sale-1' handle, page heading literally 'SALE' (the /pages/sitemap nav page links to /collections/sale, but that handle now 301-redirects with Shopify pageType=404 to the homepage -- a stale link; the live handle is sale-1). Opened and inspected: no clearance/outlet/final-sale/permanent-markdown language anywhere on the page; product tags embedded in the page's JSON are dated/rotating campaign tags such as 'Sale2023' and 'Sale Feb 2024', confirming this is a generic, periodically-refreshed promotional sale listing, not a permanent clearance/outlet concept -- excluded per the Clearance-vs-Sale test. Exact count would have been 130 (embedded product_count:130, matches exhaustive /collections/sale-1/products.json id enumeration) had it qualified. (2) 'festive-sale' handle, title 'Festive Sale', exact count 2 (embedded product_count, matches enumeration) -- a named seasonal/festive campaign tie-in, excluded as a temporary promotional sale, not clearance. Site search for 'clearance' (136 'results') and 'outlet' (60 'results') returned large non-discriminating result counts typical of this site's default/non-filtering search behavior and are themselves only search-results pages (explicitly excluded by the brief) with no underlying Clearance/Outlet PLP behind them -- confirmed by the collection sweep above. Conclusion: no genuine Clearance PLP exists on this site; nothing ambiguous enough to warrant a flagged row either (the one 'SALE' page found carries explicit rotating-campaign evidence against it, not just uncertainty).
